text:
ella: quick async — need to confirm flag resolution order for the rollout I'm wiring. route + model + project + org all have potential overrides. i'm worried about canary audiences and emergency force-off behavior. tl;dr: which wins when multiple scopes apply?

max: short answer: most-specific wins. route > model > project > org, with force-off (explicit false) at any scope taking precedence for safety. canary audiences are evaluated at the scope that set them (so a route-level canary only applies if the route flag is chosen).

raj: +1 to most-specific. to expand: if a route has a flag = null, we fall back to model; if model = null, fallback to project, etc. we should treat explicit "force-off" (flag=false && immutable) as immediate global short-circuit.

ciara: one gotcha: our current evaluation engine first resolves candidate scopes by match (route and model both match) and then picks the first non-null value by precedence. that means a route-level can set a canary audience expression, but if the route value is null and model sets a canary, the model's audience should apply. confirming this is intended?

max: yes that's intended. audience expression follows the value that was selected. so rule: 1) pick value by precedence (route/model/project/org). 2) evaluate audience expression attached to that value (if any).

ella: thanks. sample config I'm planning to use:
```
flags:
  new_reranker:
    org: { value: true }
    project: { value: null }
    model: { value: null }
    route: { value: "canary", audience: "user.segment == 'beta'" }
```
Expected behavior: route applies for beta users, org true applies for rest. correct?

raj: yep — for beta users route wins. for non-beta, route's audience fails so fall through to model/project/org and return org=true.

ciara: add a safety note: if any scope sets value=false and tags it as "force":true (emergency), we short-circuit to false even if a higher-specificity scope says true. e.g., org.force=false should still block unless route explicitly sets force=true ? we need to pick one semantic.

max: prefer semantics: any "force": true/false at a scope means that scope's value is immutable for downstream (i.e., force=false at org will override anything below). but we should restrict force flags to admins and document strongly. ops-bot: note that we'll need a migration to record existing force uses in audit logs.

ops-bot: @max created a task: INF-4321 to add audit log + admin guard rails for force flags :white_check_mark:

deply-bot: deploy planned: rollout/flags/INF-4321 will run a dry-run on staging at 22:30 UTC

ella: I'll add unit tests and a couple E2E scenarios. pinging @max for review when PR is up. also, can we add a linter to catch configs that have audience on a null value? that's a common mistake.

max: good call. i'll add a lint rule: audience expressions require non-null value at same scope or a warning if value is null (since it's probably a misconfig).

ciara: LGTM. i'll update the rollout docs with the precedence table and a small diagram.

ella: thanks all. i'll follow up with the PR link and the examples. :thumbsup:
